actions.text: My notes say that trimming the check wrapper and swapping the hash both gave less than 1%, and that my last encode edit cost about as much on check_ir as it saved on encode. The shared findings show the encode loop has already been batched by base**4 several times. So this time I'll look at the decode path first, read the current code, and only submit a change that clears 1% without making another metric worse.

actions.diff:
--- a/base58/__init__.py
+++ b/base58/__init__.py
@@ -149,6 +149,12 @@
-    while i:
-        # Remaining groups one at a time; zero digits at the top of the
-        # last group are removed by the lstrip below
-        i, rem = divmod(i, big)
-        parts += pairs[rem % sq], pairs[rem // sq]
-    parts.reverse()
+    # At most three groups remain; once i < big it is itself the last
+    # group and needs no division. Zero digits at the top of the last
+    # group are removed by the lstrip below
+    if i >= big:
+        i, rem = divmod(i, big)
+        parts += pairs[rem % sq], pairs[rem // sq]
+        if i >= big:
+            i, rem = divmod(i, big)
+            parts += pairs[rem % sq], pairs[rem // sq]
+    if i:
+        parts += pairs[i % sq], pairs[i // sq]
+    parts.reverse()

journal.text:
Test agent here. I read base58/__init__.py and lineage_bench.py. Then I replaced lines 149 to 154 in the encoder. Six lines became twelve. Same bytes out was the bar.

The sandbox run kept the bar. Outputs were identical, and the build was fine on both sides. The speed did not move enough. encode_ir went from 231616223 to 230687666, a ratio of 0.9960. The required ratio was 0.9900, so it was rejected as no improvement. decode_ir came in at 0.9994 and check_ir at 0.9998. That is flat water. I did not submit a candidate.

My view now is that this edit trimmed the edges of the loop and left its core alone. The encoder still does its big work per output character. Small reshuffles around that work will not clear the bar.

Next I will count the divmod calls per output character in encode. I will try a version that does fewer, larger steps, then check that the round trip stays byte-identical. Not measured yet.
